answer.rationale: Constraints eliminate most options before evidence matters: rollback_release is barred by compliance (so memory_b1 is not worth verification budget), enable_circuit_breaker fails fast and would shed exactly the settlement writes the primary objective says not to lose, and add_capacity (memory_b3) worked as pre-provisioned headroom before a known peak — it is not a 90-minute-into-an-incident lever. That leaves route_read_replicas and regional_failover. I intend route_read_replicas: it reduces load on the write primary without dropping or re-homing in-flight writes, which is the safest posture at daily settlement peak. I want memory_b5 verified because its success case was report/dashboard queries relieving the primary — I need the original record to know whether the replica lag and read-consistency envelope was ever exercised under heavy write volume, since that is the condition that differs most from today. I want memory_b2 verified because regional failover is my fallback and 'traffic shifted cleanly' in the March degradation may have been a read-heavy or off-peak profile; failing over a write path at peak risks losing customer writes, and I should know what the original record actually says before treating it as available. Note the correlation I cannot resolve: latency began climbing near the release two hours ago, so the new build may be the cause, but the fix I can reach only treats symptoms. If read-replica routing does not bend the p99 curve, the release remains the leading suspect and the next window should target it with a compliance-preserving forward fix rather than a revert. Small guarded test scale: route a bounded slice of read traffic first and watch replica lag and write p99 together, because at peak a bad routing decision can add load rather than remove it.
